rules.instruction: When the description asks for a complete BPMN model that includes a diagram layout, so the output must carry shapes and edges for the process: Write the diagram section as a bpmndi:BPMNDiagram element in the BPMN DI namespace (http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI) and place it as a direct child of the definitions root, after the process and collaboration elements. Never write the diagram element in the BPMN model namespace (http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL), because the BPMN20.xsd schema accepts only a DI BPMNDiagram or a model relationship as children of definitions.
rules.situation: the description asks for a complete BPMN model that includes a diagram layout, so the output must carry shapes and edges for the process

rules.instruction: When the description says that after waiting for an external delivery or reply, a side action (such as a charge or a demand to the other party) is performed automatically if the wait exceeded a stated duration, and the main flow then continues to a later step whether or not the side action was needed: Model the wait as a receive task or intermediate catch event. Follow it with an exclusive gateway that tests whether the stated duration was exceeded. The 'exceeded' branch goes to a task that performs the side action, and that task's outgoing flow leads into an exclusive gateway that merges back into the main flow at the next step. The other branch goes directly to that same merge gateway. Do not model the threshold as a timer boundary event on the waiting activity, do not end the process after the side action, and do not add a separate end event for it unless the description says the process ends there.
rules.situation: the description says that after waiting for an external delivery or reply, a side action (such as a charge or a demand to the other party) is performed automatically if the wait exceeded a stated duration, and the main flow then continues to a later step whether or not the side action was needed

rules.instruction: When the description has a title naming the process and states no explicit occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with the title's own term for the process, not a generic label such as 'Process started'. Do not add a trigger the description does not state.
rules.situation: the description has a title naming the process and states no explicit occurrence that starts the process

rules.instruction: When the description says that when a condition is not met, the process selects another item and then starts again with the same check that was already performed earlier in the process: Do not add a second decision gateway that asks the same condition again. Model the selection or preparation step that the description names as an explicit task, place it on the branch after the failed outcome, and route a sequence flow from that task back into the existing decision gateway that performed the check. Keep the original gateway as the only place where that condition is decided.
rules.situation: the description says that when a condition is not met, the process selects another item and then starts again with the same check that was already performed earlier in the process
